evidence: cfg_body_path's only failure signal is cfg_die writing to stderr, and its exit inside `$(...)` kills only the subshell, so 2>/dev/null genuinely erases the diagnostic and leaves an empty bodypath; the agent also swept the two identical suppressions at former lines 84/89 in the same commit db546db.
guidance_note: Never add a stderr suppression to a call whose failure path is a die-to-stderr helper -- the suppression deletes the only signal the caller can see.

evidence: The escaping TimeoutExpired is real, but PROVIDER_CONTRACT.md restricts every provider function to RuntimeError/CalledProcessError, so widening the generic CLI shim's catch tuple would have moved the contract boundary rather than restored it; the agent fixed it at the provider in 6ae5c6a instead.
guidance_note: When a doc declares that a module raises only X, enumerate every call inside it that can raise something else before the doc is written.

evidence: subprocess.run(timeout=...) raises TimeoutExpired, a SubprocessError sibling of CalledProcessError rather than a subclass, so it escaped _claude_once through trigger() past the contract's stated surface; the wrap in 6ae5c6a is the correct chokepoint.
guidance_note: When restoring a documented raise-surface, wrap at the one function that owns the boundary and sweep every raising call in it at once.

evidence: SKILL.md said /compact must sit in the first sentence while _first_three_sentences scanned three; aligning the doc to the more permissive implementation was the right direction, but the fix blessed placements the detector regex had never been tested against, which is exactly what F13 then reported.
guidance_note: When widening a documented input space to match an implementation, run the implementation against the newly-blessed inputs before claiming the two agree.

evidence: The file-drop arm prints `no tmux or iTerm2 transport detected` to stderr and never the `handoff scheduled` line the SKILL.md described as unconditional; the doc described only the live-transport arm.
guidance_note: When documenting a command's output, document every transport arm's output, not the happy path alone.

evidence: The file-drop arm is the last-resort never-lose-the-handoff path, and under set -e a cp into a missing ~/.claude/ aborts the script and loses the message -- the path defeats its own stated guarantee.
guidance_note: A last-resort persistence path must create its own destination directory rather than assume some other tool already made it.

evidence: The numbered steps genuinely began at 3 with no steps 1-2 anywhere in the file; the agent renumbered 3-6 to 1-4 and added a lead-in, which fixed the numbers but left the steps nested under `#### lit ready` -- the structural half the reviewer also named, and which returned three rounds later as F35. The cited law is about splitting at seams, not editing residue.
guidance_note: Dangling list numbers usually mean the list sits under the wrong heading -- do the structural move the reviewer offered as the alternative, not just the renumber.

evidence: `you want to ensure you're building on old code or going to have significant merge conflicts` literally instructs the agent to guarantee both bad outcomes; the intent was a check for overlap.
guidance_note: Prose imported wholesale into a skill gets the same line-by-line read as new code before the PR opens; this file supplied fourteen of the PR's findings.

evidence: `Skip the rest of the skill` and the immediately following backlog-pull paragraph are mutually exclusive branches with no separator, so an agent could claim the open-PR ticket and also pull a new one; the added `If there are no open PRs on the current branch:` gate closes it.
guidance_note: An instruction that says skip the rest must be followed by a paragraph opening with the complementary condition, or both branches fire.

evidence: `## General rules` was a heading with zero body; deleting it was right. The cited law governs code comments and was pasted onto an empty Markdown heading -- the reviewer's token, echoed.

release.yml:34 reads the version only from plugins/laws/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and cuts one repo-wide tag, so memento's own version field is read by nothing and can only drift; removing it is the right of the two options. Flag is a false positive -- memento's plugin.json was added by the PR's original commit, not by any fix; round 0 simply did not reach it.
guidance_note: A repo with one release tag gets one version field; a second manifest that nothing reads is drift with no reader to notice it.

evidence: The read-then-post window is real but unreachable: the provider is driven by a single sequential agent loop, so a lock would be machinery for a race the architecture cannot produce. The agent took the reviewer's own second option and documented the single-writer invariant in 2ed1f2c. Flag is a false positive -- adversarial_provider.py was in the original PR and round 0 had already reviewed line 164 of it.
guidance_note: State a single-writer invariant in a comment at the guard that depends on it, at write time, so a reviewer does not read the gap as a race.

evidence: The agent's own plan concedes the causation: `This is a direct consequence of the [earlier] fix that broadened the SKILL to within the first three sentences` -- a sentence-terminal `/compact.` became a blessed placement the regex `([[:space:]]|$)` rejects, falling through to /clear silently.
guidance_note: Before broadening where a token may appear in prose, write the matcher's accept/reject table -- which trailing characters must match and which must not -- and edit the character class once.

evidence: iTerm2's AppleScript `write` appends a newline by default (suppressed only with `newline no`), so the relaunch command submits; verified downstream at f54d9b8, where the file still has no trailing \r at `write s text` yet laws#16 added a poll that waits to read the relaunched claude's banner back out of that session -- a banner that can only appear if the write executed.
guidance_note: Where two transports differ because their APIs differ (tmux send-keys needs Enter, iTerm2 write does not), say so in a comment at the asymmetry, or the asymmetry gets re-flagged as an omission.

evidence: `Now there are no uncommitted changes` declares a state that the preceding ask-the-user branch does not establish; rewriting it as a checkpoint feeding the hard guard below is right. Flag is a false positive -- the line appears verbatim as unchanged original text in the round-0 diff hunks of F9 and F10, so no fix produced it. The cited law is about seams, not false assertions in prose.
guidance_note: A line that asserts a precondition (`now there are no X`) should be written as the check that establishes it.

evidence: The bullet `Acceptance criteria missing or vague? Ask.` and the paragraph below it (`only a good question if it's not clearly answerable`) give opposite instructions for the same condition, and both appear unchanged in the round-0 hunks -- pre-existing, not caused by a fix. The token is decoration on a contradiction, which is a one-source-of-truth shape at best.
guidance_note: When a checklist bullet and the paragraph beneath it answer the same condition differently, one of them is dead -- resolve it when the file is written.

evidence: The reviewer named two acceptable remedies -- expand the section with distinct scenarios, or merge the one scenario back and delete the heading -- and the agent did neither, changing `a couple of scenarios` to `one scenario` in 0a56955. The duplicate-content complaint survived untouched and returned as F22 one round later.
guidance_note: When a reviewer names the acceptable remedies explicitly, fixing the wording instead of taking one of them buys a repeat finding.

evidence: A checkable factual claim: the parenthetical named local and adversarial as setup_check False while both manifests declare it True (adversarial_provider.py:34, local_provider.py:24), which the agent confirmed and removed. Flag is a false positive -- the SKILL.md line was in the PR's original commit and round 2 simply re-scoped onto address-pr-reviews.
guidance_note: Do not restate a CAPABILITIES dict's values in prose; point at the dict, which cannot go stale against itself.

evidence: F13's fix enumerated exactly `[.!?]`, so `/compact,` and `/compact:` -- equally natural placements under the same broadened SKILL.md guidance -- still fell through to /clear; the third edit of the same six-character class in three rounds.
guidance_note: Fixing a matcher by adding the two characters a reviewer named, rather than the boundary the token actually needs, guarantees the next character shows up as the next round's finding.

evidence: message-in-a-bottle's SKILL.md, added in this same PR, instructs callers to pass --goal when a goal is active, and address-pr-reviews' Finalize step, also added in this PR, omits it -- a caller violating a contract that landed beside it. The law token was written into the doc note rather than applied: nothing enforces the goal-carry, which is what single-enforcer would be about. Flag is a false positive; both files are original to the PR.
guidance_note: When one PR adds both a contract and its caller, grep the caller for every required argument the contract names before opening the PR.

evidence: PREPATORY is a non-word; it appears unchanged in the round-0 and round-1 diff hunks, so the fix-commit flag is a false positive -- the typo was original text the reviewer reached in round 2.

The reviewer re-raised the identical complaint one round later because F17's fix changed only the scenario count; the agent then did what was asked the first time, dropping the duplicated scenario and leaving a pointer to the Uncommitted changes section.
guidance_note: A repeat of the same finding one round later is the signal that the previous fix addressed the sentence and not the defect; take the named remedy first time.

evidence: The mode comment declared `--worker <target> <reset> <msgfile>` while the launcher passes four arguments including GOALFILE, and `--iterm-worker` was short by the same argument; the whole file is new in this PR (hunk header `@@ -0,0 +1,389 @@`), so the drift was original, not produced by a fix -- the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Adding a positional argument to an internal worker protocol and its usage comment is one edit, not two.

evidence: F19's fix replaced the enumerated class with `[[:punct:]]`, which includes `-`, so `/compact-cache` newly matched and would trigger a compaction reset it never triggered before -- a case that worked under the prior class and stopped working. The agent's final `[.,:;!?]` is the set that satisfies both rounds.
guidance_note: Widening a character class to fix a missed accept must be checked against the reject set too -- write both columns before editing the class.

evidence: `pull from orphans first` and `If there aren't any other tickets, take from the top of the ready queue` are not mutually exclusive as written, so an agent can pull two tickets; both sentences appear unchanged in the round-0 hunks, so the fix-commit flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Every `do X first` branch needs its `otherwise` partner written at the same time, or the two arms both fire.

evidence: Not a bug -- an open PR is not a ticket, and the plugin ships address-pr-reviews for exactly that branch, so `proceed to work that ticket` under-specified the route; the fix is a one-line improvement, not a defect repair. Pre-existing text; flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When the same plugin ships the skill that handles a branch, route to it by name from that branch.

evidence: Both worked examples use `git checkout -b`, which fails outright on a resumed ticket whose branch exists -- the common case for the orphaned-ticket path the same file tells the agent to prefer. Pre-existing text; flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: A worked `git checkout -b` example in agent guidance needs its already-exists arm, because resuming a ticket is the normal case.

evidence: The overlap check told the agent to look for a conflict and named no action on finding one. The flag is a false positive as causation: the actionless check predates F8's rewrite, which only made the garbled sentence legible -- but F8's fix touched this exact sentence and stopped short of finishing it.
guidance_note: When rewriting an instruction to be legible, finish it -- a check with no stated action on a positive result is still incomplete.

evidence: marketplace.json advertised `code / prose / prompt / ticket` while the laws manifest lists three and ticket ships as DISABLED_SKILL.md; the PR edited that entry's source path without checking the description beside it. The round-2 summary had already noted this as unanchored, so the reviewer carried it for two rounds before anchoring it -- not caused by any fix.
guidance_note: When a PR edits one field of a marketplace or manifest entry, check the whole entry against what it advertises, not only the field being changed.

evidence: The test was not broken -- 8f6d15b does resolve, as F31's fix then relies on -- so the reviewer's `passes for the wrong reason` overstates a fragility: cfg_validate would abort first only if that ref ever stopped resolving. Pinning HEAD is still the right fix. Pre-existing test; flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: A negative test must pin its inputs so the abort can only originate in the arm the test is named for.

evidence: The PR's own new logic is the dual-location fallback in cfg_body_path, and every assertion exercised only HEAD -- the new-location arm; the old-location arm that the whole change exists for had no assertion at all. Pre-existing gap in the PR, not from a fix.
guidance_note: When you add a fallback branch to a lookup, add the assertion that reaches the fallback in the same commit -- the primary arm's test does not cover it.

evidence: The diff hunk shows json.loads(proc.stdout) sitting directly below the try/except TimeoutExpired that F3's fix installed: the same off-contract escape from the same function, in the same raise-surface, that the earlier sweep did not cover. json.JSONDecodeError is a ValueError and escapes trigger() exactly as TimeoutExpired did.
guidance_note: When wrapping one exception to restore a documented raise-surface, enumerate every call in that function that can raise off-contract -- subprocess.run and json.loads both do -- and wrap them in one commit.

evidence: The gap is real -- a fixed CLAUDE_BOOT_SECONDS=6 with the worker logging `carried goal re-established` unconditionally is a silent failure -- but both proposed remedies were wrong (a bigger magic number lowers the probability without closing it; a verified retry is a feature). The agent filed promptctl-handoff-6h7 and shipped the readiness probe as laws#16, opened 18 minutes later.
guidance_note: A fixed sleep standing in for a readiness signal is a defect at write time, especially when the sibling transport in the same file already reads its pane back.

evidence: `Check for open PRs related to your current branch?` gave no command while the same file gives concrete git commands elsewhere, and lit ready lists tickets rather than PRs -- an agent that checks only lit misses the in-flight PR and starts duplicate work. Pre-existing text; flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: An instruction to check for X must carry the exact command, and must say which tool does not surface X.

evidence: F7's fix renumbered the steps and added a lead-in but left them nested under `#### lit ready`, which is inside `the rest of the skill` that three separate branches tell the agent to skip; the agent finally promoted them to a top-level `## Working the ticket` section and rewrote every skip directive to point at it -- the structural remedy F7's reviewer had offered as its first option.
guidance_note: If steps must be reachable from every entry path, they belong in a top-level section -- promote them the first time rather than patching the numbers that dangle because of the nesting.

narrative: A 2394-line plugin-extraction PR that took five review rounds and 35 advisory findings, all resolved, none blocking. Six findings (F13, F19, F22, F24, F32, F35) exist only because an earlier fix was narrow: the /compact matcher was edited in four consecutive rounds (F4 broadened the doc, F13 added [.!?], F19 replaced it with [[:punct:]], F24 caught that [[:punct:]] admits the hyphen), F17's word-count fix drew the identical complaint back as F22, F7's renumber left the structure that returned as F35, and F3's exception wrap swept one of two off-contract raises in the same function. avoidable_rounds is nonetheless 0 by the strict test: every round after the first also carried independent findings on text the PR never changed, so no round would have vanished. The bulk of the review's volume is the two SKILL.md files imported wholesale -- roughly twenty of the 35 findings are prose-structure defects in text the agent never read as carefully as it read its own code.
guidance_observations: The reviewer re-reads unchanged files every round and surfaces fresh pre-existing findings each time, so fix-completeness alone cannot shorten a PR like this -- the lever is a pre-PR read of every prose file the PR adds wholesale, at the same standard as the code.

Where the agent swept siblings unprompted (F1's two extra 2>/dev/null instances, in the same commit) no follow-on finding appeared; where it fixed only the cited line (F7, F13, F17, F19) the finding came back.

Three of the four caused-chains are one predicate or one section being re-edited round after round, which is what happens when a fix is written from the reviewer's example rather than from the full accept/reject set.

The reviewer attached [LAW:decomposition] to nine prose nits and the agent echoed the token back in its own plan on five of them (F7, F9, F15, F16, F17), only one of which (F9, two branches with no separator) is actually a seam problem -- law citations here track the reviewer's vocabulary rather than the argument being made.

Two findings (F2, F12) were answered by taking a different remedy than the reviewer's primary one, both correctly and both accepted in one round, which is evidence the different_fix path is working as intended.

evidence: The healthy read writes nothing to stderr (session found returns text, absent UUID returns empty at exit 0), so 2>/dev/null could only suppress genuine AppleScript faults -- the exact diagnostic missing when the 30s poll reports a bare timeout; the worker's stderr already lands in the log via nohup, and the file's two other osascript calls use 2>>/dev/stderr.
guidance_note: Before silencing a call inside a poll loop to avoid spam, check whether the healthy path writes to stderr at all -- if it does not, the suppression only hides faults.

narrative: The follow-through on laws#15/F33's deferral: it replaces the fixed 6-second boot sleep in the iTerm2 goal-carry with a readiness poll that reads the relaunched claude's banner back out of the session, and surfaces a failure instead of logging success on timeout. One advisory finding, accepted with an argument that reasoned from what the healthy path actually writes rather than from consistency alone, fixed in f54d9b8; round 1 found nothing. This is the clean counterexample to laws#15 in the same batch.
guidance_observations: Deferring laws#15/F33 into its own small PR produced a one-finding, two-round review, which is direct evidence that the pushback-plus-ticket answer was right rather than avoidance.
The accepted-fix reply that states why the agent's original instinct was wrong (rather than only what changed) is the shape that closes a thread in one round.

evidence: The reviewer is factually right that the path does not resolve, and the agent does not dispute it -- it disputes fixing one instance. I fetched .claude/skills/laws/SKILL.md at 77710fc: the same plugin-root-relative convention appears at lines 3, 22, 27, 41 and 58, so the agent's enumeration is accurate and a line-41-only fix would leave one repo-relative path among five plugin-relative siblings. Filed as promptctl-docs-0qf.
guidance_note: A skill body that ships to both .claude/skills/ and plugins/ must state which root its internal paths are relative to, in the file, or every reader resolves them differently.

narrative: A single-commit change to the craft guard's compatibility model, one advisory finding, one round. The finding was a genuinely broken relative path that the PR did not introduce; the agent pushed back with the enumeration of the five sibling paths sharing the convention, the reason a one-line fix would make things worse, and a ticket. Verified against the file at that commit -- the enumeration holds.
guidance_observations: A pushback that enumerates the sibling instances, names why the narrow fix is a new inconsistency, and files the ticket is the form that ends a pre-existing-defect thread in one round.

The review summary also flagged a stale `Never load a second craft in the same session` line that contradicts the PR's new rule 1, but it appears only in the round summary and was never anchored as a thread, so nothing in the packet shows whether it was fixed.

evidence: The doc rests its ban on 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-01 sensitivity campaign data whose only source, evals/suites/code/SENSITIVITY.md, is deleted by the same commit, and the Salvage section names a git-history recovery path for the isolation and driver code but not for the records. The thread has no replies and is still unresolved; the PR was merged at 07:44:29, eight minutes before the review posted at 07:52:55.
guidance_note: When a doc's justification cites data the same commit deletes, name the recovery ref for that data in the same paragraph as the claim.

narrative: A 3982-line deletion of the single-session eval tree plus the policy doc that bans it. The review found one real advisory gap -- the policy cites empirical records that the same commit removes -- and it was never answered, because the PR was merged two minutes after it was opened and eight minutes before the review landed. The finding is open to this day.
guidance_observations: Merging before the review posts makes every finding on that PR unaddressed by construction; the guidance gap is not in how findings are answered but in whether the merge waits for the review at all.

A deletion PR gets its review value from what the deleted tree was still supporting -- here a cited evidence base -- which is the one thing a diff-shaped review can see and the author did not check before deleting.

evidence: The premise is right and was later vindicated: the file's own dual-secret-store comment block at ece684a named only DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, and today's master carries the same block rewritten around `${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}` -- the invariant did need extending. The thread got no reply and is unresolved; the PR merged three seconds after opening, four minutes before the review posted.
guidance_note: When a change adds a second secret to a workflow that documents a dual-store invariant for the first, extend the invariant in the same edit -- and make it in the generating template, since this file's own header says the installer overwrites local edits.

evidence: The supply-chain mechanism is real but the framing is weak here: copirate-code-review-agent is a first-party action in the same promptctl org as the repo, and the mutable @v1 pin still stands on master two weeks later, so the recommendation was declined in practice without ever being answered. The file is also GENERATED -- its header reads `do not edit by hand ... the installer reconverges it on every run` -- so the pin cannot be changed in this repo at all.
guidance_note: A finding on a generated file needs a reply naming the template as the only editable source; silence is indistinguishable from having missed it.

narrative: A one-line CI fix, merged three seconds after it was opened and reviewed four minutes later, so both findings arrived on a merged PR and neither was ever answered or resolved. F1's substance was genuine and was closed later upstream in the installer template, which now documents the dual-secret-store invariant for CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. F2's SHA-pin recommendation was never adopted; master still uses @v1. Both findings sit on a file whose own header forbids hand edits, which is the answer the threads needed and never got.
guidance_observations: Two of the five PRs in this batch merged before their review posted, and both produced findings with zero replies -- the review round is being spent with no channel back to the author.

Findings anchored on generated files (this workflow, and anything else install.sh reconverges) need a standing answer that points at the template; without it the reviewer will re-raise them on every repo the installer touches.
